arte.universo: London between 1820 and 1843: an elegant English drawing room with a piano, heavy curtains and bookshelves, a candle-lit study with a wooden desk covered in handwritten papers, a Victorian salon with a large brass calculating machine made of stacked columns of gears, a dim inventor's workshop with huge technical drawings of gears and wheels pinned to the walls; and a modern Mexican teenager's bedroom at night today. No portraits and no recognizable real people: the mathematician and the inventor are never shown, only their objects and places. Anonymous people only from behind or far away. No readable writing, letters or digits anywhere.

escena.accion: At night in a candle-lit Victorian study, the Pasita stands beside a wooden desk covered in stacks of handwritten papers and drawings of gears; on the desk a small brass model of interlocking gear wheels glows softly lime green, as if it were alive
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, seen from behind, small school backpack, looking at the glowing brass gears
escena.objeto: A small brass model of interlocking gear wheels with a soft lime-green glow, papers with only abstract lines and diagrams (no letters, no digits)
escena.foreground: The edge of the desk with a quill pen and an inkwell, slightly blurred
escena.background: Tall dark bookshelves and a window with foggy London night and gas street lamps
escena.iluminacion: A single candle and the lime glow of the gears, deep blue shadows
escena.emocion: Mystery and wonder: the future in an old room
escena.composicion: Medium-wide shot from behind; the upper 42% is the calm dark wall and ceiling of the study for the title

cuerpo: Su mamá la puso a estudiar **matemáticas**.

escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, three-quarter view from behind, backpack on the chair, holding a drawing compass
escena.objeto: An open book with geometric figures only (no letters, no digits), a brass drawing compass and a small slate
escena.foreground: The carved back of an armchair, slightly blurred
escena.background: A piano with a closed leather book, heavy curtains, a tall window with grey English daylight
escena.iluminacion: Soft grey daylight from the window, warm shadows
escena.composicion: Medium shot; the upper 42% dark calm wall with picture frames in shadow

escena.accion: In a Victorian salon in the evening, the Pasita stands in front of a large shining brass calculating machine made of stacked columns of gear wheels and a hand crank, while a few anonymous elegant guests stand far away, seen only from behind
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, seen from behind, backpack on, looking up at the brass machine in awe
escena.objeto: A tall brass calculating machine with columns of gear wheels and a crank handle (wheels without visible digits)
escena.foreground: A velvet rope and the edge of a chair, slightly blurred

cuerpo: Nunca se construyó: **solo existía en papel**.

escena.accion: In a dim inventor's workshop, the Pasita looks at huge technical drawings of gears, wheels and levers pinned all over the walls and spread on a long table, with a few loose brass gears lying unused beside them
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, seen from behind, backpack on, standing small in front of the giant drawings
escena.objeto: Enormous technical drawings of a gear machine made only of lines and circles (no letters, no digits) and loose brass gears

cuerpo: y le agregó notas **tres veces más largas**.

escena.accion: Late at night at a wooden desk, the Pasita sits on a chair and looks at a small thin printed booklet next to a much taller stack of handwritten pages, with a quill in an inkwell and a candle burning low
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, three-quarter view from behind, backpack on the floor, resting a hand on the tall stack of pages

escena.foreground: The candle and the inkwell, slightly blurred
escena.background: Dark bookshelves and a window with foggy night
escena.iluminacion: One low candle, warm light on the papers, deep shadows
escena.composicion: Medium shot; the upper 42% dark wall and ceiling

cuerpo: Paso a paso, para calcular **números de Bernoulli**.

escena.accion: In a modern Mexican teenager's bedroom at night, the Pasita sits at a desk with a laptop showing only colorful sound waves and blocks, wearing headphones; beside the laptop a small antique brass gear wheel glows softly lime green
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, seen from behind, backpack hanging on the chair, headphones on
escena.objeto: A laptop screen with abstract colorful sound waves (no letters, no digits) and a small antique brass gear with a lime glow
escena.foreground: A desk lamp and a phone with headphones cable, slightly blurred
escena.background: Posters with only abstract shapes, a window with the warm lights of a Mexican city at night

escena.composicion: Medium-wide shot; the upper 42% dark calm wall of the bedroom

post:
Ada Lovelace nació en Londres en 1815. Era hija del poeta Lord Byron, y su mamá la puso a estudiar matemáticas desde niña. 🧮

En 1833, a los 17 años, conoció a Charles Babbage y vio funcionar su máquina de calcular. Babbage diseñó después otra mucho más poderosa, la Máquina Analítica, que nunca se llegó a construir.

En 1843 Ada tradujo un artículo sobre esa máquina y le agregó notas tres veces más largas que el original. En la Nota G escribió, paso a paso, cómo la máquina calcularía los números de Bernoulli: se le considera el primer programa publicado de la historia (Babbage había hecho borradores que nunca publicó). Hoy se sabe que tenía un pequeño error… como cualquier código. 😅 También imaginó que esas máquinas podrían componer música.

Lo que haces en Tecnología con algoritmos y diagramas de flujo empezó con unas notas escritas a mano hace más de 180 años.
